source.name: Open-access article (calculated values)
source.reference: V. Jerabek, V. Stejfa, M. Klajmon, K. Rehak, Thermodynamic Properties and Phase Equilibria of Dihydrolevoglucosenone and Its Mixtures with Hydrocarbons, J. Chem. Eng. Data 68 (2023) 3361-3376, doi:10.1021/acs.jced.3c00461, Table 4
source.access: Open access, CC BY 4.0 (American Chemical Society)
source.notes: Values calculated, not measured: rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator (RRHO) model with quantum-chemistry molecular data of the stable conformer (Table S1 of the supporting information); expanded uncertainty (k = 2) 0.01 Cp as stated; the authors check it against their calorimetric liquid heat capacities and vapour pressures (SimCor, section 3.6). Used instead of the databank: the ChemSep v8.31 data 2 value is about as large as the measured liquid heat capacity (190 against 200 J/(mol K) at 298 K, Jerabek et al. 2023, Table 3), where the calculated ideal-gas value is 75 J/(mol K) lower; the ChemSep v8.31 pure-component database, data file 2 value at 298.15 K, 189.8 J/(mol K), is +52 % from it.

source.name: measured vapour pressures (2 open-access articles) and the critical point
source.fit: Fitted to measured vapour pressures (2 open-access articles): 49 values with stated uncertainties within 1 % from 1 articles, max deviation 0.29 %, and 44 values with larger stated uncertainties, kept where the fit is within them (they extend the range to 253.26 K); and the ChemSep v8.31 pure-component database, data file 2 critical point (657.86 K, 3566445 Pa). Between 403.16 K and the critical point the curve is held only by the critical point. ChemSep stores the vapour pressure in its equation 200, which DWSIM, the open-source program that redistributes the databank, does not define (PropertyPackage.vb, CalcCSTDepProp: no case for it), so it was not used. Articles: Jerabek et al., J. Chem. Eng. Data 68 (2023) 3361-3376, doi:10.1021/acs.jced.3c00461; Baird et al., Int. J. Thermophys. 40 (2019) 102, doi:10.1007/s10765-019-2570-9. Rules: validation/python/measured_components.py (fit_measured_loose).
